- Overestimate near recent peaks; model tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes.
- Underestimate in early part of forecast horizon; model often starts too high and then drops.
- Exhibit mean reversion bias: model fails to recognize that prices often revert to recent 10-15 day average after strong moves.
- Lagged response: model reacts too slowly to new data; true values often shift faster than forecasted.
- Overconfident in short-term volatility; model overweights recent noise and underweights long-term trend.
- High variance in forecast tails; model frequently overpredicts extreme values (especially above 80) and underpredicts sharp drops.
- Avoid extrapolating from 30-day history without smoothing; model is prone to “memory decay” errors when history is noisy.
- Correct for “forecast drift”: if model consistently forecasts higher than true values in last 5-7 days, reduce forecast by 1-2% per day.
- Use moving average of last 7 days as a sanity check; if forecast deviates > 3% from this, adjust downward.
